kevin: heads-up — seeing weird KV cache residency DECAY on Mistral runs when rope crosses a boundary (around 2048->4096). pages keep getting reused then evicted in quick succession. repro on dev-gpu-3. :eyes:

alex: ok — short summary and a minimal repro please? can you paste the runtime counters and any kernel-selection logs.

kevin: repro command I used:

```
./run_kv_repro --model=mistral-8x --rope=4096 --seq=32768 --concurrent=4 --workload=mix_long_short
```

logs show repeated lines like:
```
[kv] page_reuse miss p=0x7f9a2c4a cnt=17 age=3
[kv] alloc page=1248 size=256 owner=beam-123
[kv] page_evicted id=1248 reason=low_residency
```

marta: short/quick thought — sounds like small short requests are interleaving and preventing long contexts from accumulating prefix KV, so we never hit a steady residency and pages churn. batching heuristics might be merging tiny requests which increases collision.

sara: can you try `--disable-auto-batching` and `--kv-page-size=512`? also check if kernel selection is switching to a fallback kernel for MQA vs GQA; that can change memory access patterns.

kevin: tried disable-batching — churn drops but p99 latency jumps; not acceptable. kernel-selection log (excerpt):

```
2026-03-17T16:45:02Z kernel_select: seq_len=4096 chosen=attn_mqa_fast revision=3 reason=tile_mismatch
2026-03-17T16:45:02Z kernel_select: seq_len=8192 chosen=generic_matmul fallback=true
```

so when rope scaling pushes seq_len into the higher bucket we fall back to generic kernels which do different paging access (strided vs tiled).

jonas: also check rope table indexing — we had one bug where the rope offset calculation wrapped at 4096 for certain layer counts, effectively causing KV keys to alias across layers (bad for reuse). could be layer-level collisions -> early eviction heuristics think page is low residency.

kevin: interesting — i'll run a pagewalk/heapmap and post. quick vmstat-ish telemetry from the run: `rss=62GB anon=48GB kv_pages=2100 kv_residency_avg=0.12 kv_reuse_hits=120 kv_reuse_misses=485`

alex: can you capture `env=INFER_DEBUG=1 ./run_kv_repro ...` and attach the `kv_page_walk` output? also a short perf sample: `perf record -F 99 -g -- ./run_kv_repro ...; perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded` — a flame would help.

kevin: attaching small snippet inline — page_walk shows many adjacent pages with residency=1 and short ages:

```
page 1246: age=2 residency=1 last_owner=beam-121
page 1247: age=1 residency=1 last_owner=beam-45
page 1248: age=0 residency=0 last_owner=beam-123 evicted=1
page 1249: age=3 residency=2 last_owner=beam-121
```

marta: hmm looks like rapid age resets. that suggests the sweep/decay timer might be firing too aggressively under this mixed workload. was the recent sweep timer change deployed to runtime-stable last week?

infra-bot: deploy: runtime-stable v2026.3.14 rolled out to dev-gpu-3 at 2026-03-16T04:12Z (flags: kv-sweep-ms=500, kv-residency-threshold=0.4)

kevin: flag `kv-sweep-ms=500` — that is probably too aggressive for long contexts. will re-run with `kv-sweep-ms=2000` and `kv-residency-threshold=0.2` to see if residency stabilizes.

sara: keep kernel-selection logs on — if fallback to generic_matmul persists we may need a quantization/tile tweak rather than disabling kernels. also try `--kv-alloc-strategy=clustered` to bias allocations to the same slab.

jonas: for cross-model check: Qwen's MQA path uses a different key-layout; if MQA->GQA mode toggle happens mid-run (model variant auto-switching), that could explain misaligned keys. verify model variant pinning.

kevin: plan: 1) run with larger sweep interval + clustered alloc 2) capture heapmap + perf flame 3) confirm rope offset math across layers 4) test Qwen with same flags. i'll post results shortly.

alex: great — thanks. if you reproduce, open a perf ticket and drop the `perf.folded` + pagewalk dump. label `priority=high` for Dedicated customers. :thumbsup:
